newsitem.title: UK: Key world closing stock market indices, July 25.
newsitem.headline: Key world closing stock market indices, July 25.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 index failed to make any progress after a subdued performance on Wall Street and ahead of an onslaught of major company earnings. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,851.5, down 11.4 points, or 0.23 percent. The index was down 25.7 from last week.

FRANKFURT - Shares closed a lacklustre floor session down nearly half a percent but bounced back into positive territory in late trade, capping a record-breaking week. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,317.64, down 18.10 points, or 0.42 percent, giving a rise of 121.11 on the week. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,368.54, up 48.02 points, or 1.11 percent.

PARIS - Stocks set a new closing record after an advance fuelled by the dollar's strength. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,025.94, up 52.41 points, or 1.76 percent on the day and rising 149.25 points from last week.

ZURICH - Shares ended little changed in quiet pre-weekend trade as the positive effect of a firmer dollar was offset by some profit-taking. The Swiss market index closed at 5,847.0, down 2.2 points, or 0.04 percent. There was a rise of 109.9 on the week.

MILAN - Shares closed firmer with support coming from a higher Dow Jones and the slightly firmer trend to domestic bonds, with investors still prepared to buy on any weakness in the market, dealers said. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 15,094, up 88 points, or 0.58 percent, gaining 553 points on the week.

AMSTERDAM - Shares swung higher in late trade to end a lacklustre session in positive territory after Wall Street's firmer opening kindled fresh enthusiasm. The AEX index closed at 989.03, up 3.78 points, or 0.38 percent. There was a rise of 47.24 from last week.

TOKYO - Stocks finished moderately higher, as some blue-chip issues drew support from Wall Street's record climb, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,389.54, up 103.31 points, or 0.51 percent. This was up 140.22 from last Friday.

HONG KONG - Stocks slipped to a moderately lower close on profit-taking in the market's defensive sectors, and the index was likely to continue to trend weaker on regional currency worries, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,658.12, down 51.11 points, or 0.33 percent, for a rise of 87.72 on the week.

SYDNEY - The share market ended 0.55 percent higher, supported by overseas gains and general expectations of an official interest rate cut in the next few weeks. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,691.2, up 14.8 points on the day and showing a rise of seven points from the previous Friday's close.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended a busy week with another day of heavy trade that saw the industrials index hit a new high as local buyers poured into the market, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,444.0, up 17.0 points, or 0.23 percent and up 19.1 from a week ago. The All Gold index closed at 969.8, up 17.2 points, or 0.31 percent, but falling 22.2 since last week. The Industrial index closed at 9,054.4, up 28.1 points, or 1.81 percent and rising 116.7 points from last Friday.
